# **Definition and Acronyms**  {#definition-and-acronyms}

| Acronym/ Term | Definition |
| :---: | ----- |
| CMS | **Cinema Management System** – the web-based system used to manage movie browsing, ticket booking, payments, cinema operations, accounts, and related functions.  |
| SRS  |  **Software Requirements Specification** – the document that describes the system scope, functional requirements, business rules, use cases, actors, and other system requirements.  |
| UC  | **Use Case** – a description of an interaction between an actor and the system to achieve a specific goal.  |
| BR  | **Business Rule** – a rule or constraint that governs system behavior and business operations.  |
| BF  | **Business Flow** – an end-to-end workflow describing how a business process is performed in the system.  |
| ERD  | **Entity Relationship Diagram –** a diagram showing the system entities and the relationships between them.  |
| OTP  | **One-Time Password –** a temporary verification code used for email verification and password recovery.  |
| QR Code  | **Quick Response Code** – a machine-readable code generated for a ticket and used during ticket verification and cinema check-in.  |
| F\&B  | **Food and Beverage** – food, drink, and combo items that may be selected during online or counter ticket booking.  |
| API  | **Application Programming Interface** – an interface that allows the Cinema Management System to communicate with external services.  |
| Payment Gateway  | An external payment service used by the Cinema Management System to process electronic payment transactions and return payment results.  |
| VNPay  | The payment service used or simulated by the project for processing online payments and payment callbacks.  |
| Webhook  | A mechanism through which an external service, such as the Payment Gateway, sends transaction results back to the Cinema Management System automatically.  |
| Email Service  | An external service used to send OTP codes, password recovery emails, booking confirmations, digital ticket information, and other notifications.  |
| POS  | **Point of Sale** – the counter-sale environment used by Staff for ticket payment, receipt printing, and physical ticket printing.  |
| VAT  | **Value Added Tax** – an optional tax that may be included in the final booking amount if enabled by system configuration.  |
| HMAC-SHA512  | A cryptographic signature mechanism used to validate payment callback data from VNPay.  |
| URL  | **Uniform Resource Locator** – the address used to identify an API endpoint or web resource.  |
| RBAC  | **Role-Based Access Control** – an authorization approach in which system permissions are granted according to assigned roles such as Customer, Staff, Manager, and Admin.  |
| N/A  | **Not Applicable** – indicates that a field or item does not apply in a particular context.  |

# **I. Overall Requirements** {#i.-overall-requirements}

## **1\. Context Diagram** {#1.-context-diagram}

*The Cinema Management System is a centralized, role-based web application for movie browsing, ticket booking, payment, ticket verification, and cinema operations. The system supports five main roles: Guest, Customer, Staff, Manager, and Admin. Guests can browse movies, showtimes, promotions and news, register accounts, and authenticate. Customers can book tickets, select seats and optional F\&B items or vouchers, make payments, receive digital tickets with QR codes, view booking and transaction history, manage profile information, view loyalty information, and submit movie reviews. Staff handle counter ticket sales, member lookup, ticket printing, ticket verification, age eligibility verification, and news submission. Managers manage movies, cinema rooms, seat types and layouts, showtimes, ticket pricing, food and beverage items, promotions and vouchers, reports, and news approval. Admins manage customer accounts, Staff and Manager accounts, roles, permissions, and system configuration. The system integrates with a Payment Gateway for payment processing and an Email Service for OTP, password recovery, booking confirmation, ticket information, and other notifications.*

## **2\. Main Business Flow** {#2.-main-business-flow}

### **2.1 Account Registration & Authentication (BF-01)**  {#2.1-account-registration-&-authentication-(bf-01)}

**Trigger:** A user starts account registration, authentication process.

**End condition:** The account is successfully created and verified, or the user successfully logs in.

![][image3]

### **2.2 Online Ticket Booking (BF-02)**  {#2.2-online-ticket-booking-(bf-02)}

**Trigger:** Customer selects a movie and starts the ticket booking process.

**End condition:** Payment is completed successfully and the digital ticket is issued, or the booking ends because payment is unsuccessful.

## **3\. Conceptual Data Model** {#3.-conceptual-data-model}

### **3.1 Entity Relationship Diagram** {#3.1-entity-relationship-diagram}

![][image8]

### **3.2 Entity Descriptions** {#3.2-entity-descriptions}

**Entity: Role** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a system role used to determine the type of access granted to an account.  |
| Key business attributes | Role name, description  |
| Business identity | Role names must be unique across the system. Typical roles are Customer, Staff, Manager, and Admin.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Roles are predefined or maintained by Admin. No separate lifecycle is required.  |

**Entity: Permission** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an individual system permission that may be assigned to one or more roles.  |
| Key business attributes | Permission name, description  |
| Business identity | Permission name must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | No independent lifecycle is required.  |

**Entity: RolePermission** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Associates Roles with the Permissions they are allowed to use.  |
| Key business attributes | Role, Permission  |
| Business identity | The combination of RoleID and PermissionID must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Created when a permission is assigned to a role and removed when the assignment is revoked.  |

**Entity: Account**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a system user account used for authentication, authorization, and account status management.  |
| Key business attributes | Role, username, email, password hash, full name, phone number, status, created date  |
| Business identity | Username, email, and phone number must be unique. Each Account is assigned to one Role.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending Verification → Active → Locked / Inactive. Only Active accounts may successfully authenticate.  |

**Entity: Customer** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Stores business information specific to a registered cinema customer.  |
| Key business attributes | Account, date of birth, address, membership rank, available points, tier points, promotion-email preference  |
| Business identity | Each Customer must be associated with exactly one Account, and one Account may have at most one Customer profile.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Customer availability follows the associated Account status. Membership rank may change according to loyalty rules.  |

**Entity: Staff** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Stores information specific to a cinema Staff account used for counter sales, ticket verification, and news creation.  |
| Key business attributes | Account, position, staff status  |
| Business identity | Each Staff record belongs to exactly one Account.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive. Access also depends on the linked Account status.  |

**Entity: Movie** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a movie managed and displayed by the cinema system.  |
| Key business attributes | Title, duration, release date, language, director, age rating, description, poster, trailer, status  |
| Business identity | No natural unique key is required; multiple movies may have similar titles. MovieID uniquely identifies each movie.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Managed according to movie availability, such as upcoming, available/showing, ended, or archived.  |

**Entity: Genre** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a movie genre used to classify movies.  |
| Key business attributes | Genre name  |
| Business identity | Genre name must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | No special lifecycle is required unless genres are administratively disabled.  |

**Entity: MovieGenre** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents the many-to-many classification between Movies and Genres.  |
| Key business attributes | Movie, Genre  |
| Business identity | The combination of MovieID and GenreID must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Created or removed when Manager updates a movie's genres.  |

**Entity: MovieReview** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Stores ratings and comments submitted by eligible Customers for Movies.  |
| Key business attributes | Customer, Movie, rating, review content, status, created date  |
| Business identity | ReviewID uniquely identifies each review. The system may restrict a Customer to one review per Movie.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active or hidden/disabled according to moderation rules.  |

**Entity: Room** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a cinema screening room in which showtimes are scheduled.  |
| Key business attributes | Room name, room type, capacity, status  |
| Business identity | Room name must be unique within the cinema system.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive. Inactive rooms cannot receive new showtimes.  |

**Entity: SeatType** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Defines seat classifications that affect seat pricing and customer experience.  |
| Key business attributes | Type name, description, price multiplier, status  |
| Business identity | The seat type name must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive. Existing seat records may retain their assigned type.  |

 **\=\> Examples may include Standard, Front, VIP, and Couple.** 

**Entity: Seat**  

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a physical seat configured in a cinema room. |
| Key business attributes | Room, seat type, row label, seat number, grid row, grid column, status  |
| Business identity | A seat position/number must be unique within its Room.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive/Unavailable.  |

 **\=\> GridRow and GridColumn support the seat-layout configuration; unused grid positions can represent aisles.**


**Entity: Showtime** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a scheduled screening of a Movie in a Room at a specific time.  |
| Key business attributes | Movie, Room, start time, end time, base ticket price, status  |
| Business identity | ShowtimeID uniquely identifies a screening. A Room must not contain overlapping showtimes.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Scheduled/Active → Completed or Inactive/Cancelled according to cinema operations.  |

**Entity: Booking** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an online or counter ticket booking for one Showtime.  |
| Key business attributes | Customer (optional for counter sale), Staff (optional for online sale), Showtime, Voucher, booking code, booking type, subtotal, discount, tax, total amount, booking time, status  |
| Business identity | BookingCode must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending → Paid/Confirmed; Pending may expire if payment is not completed within the seat-hold period.  |

 **\=\> BookingType identifies whether the booking was made ONLINE or at the COUNTER.** 

**Entity: BookingSeat** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a Seat selected and temporarily held or purchased as part of a Booking.  |
| Key business attributes | Booking, Seat, unit price, hold expiration time, status  |
| Business identity | The same Seat must not be simultaneously held or booked by multiple active Bookings for the same Showtime.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Held → Booked when payment succeeds; Held → Released/Expired when the hold period expires.  |

**Entity: Ticket** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents the digital or physical ticket issued for a successfully purchased BookingSeat.  |
| Key business attributes | BookingSeat, QR code, ticket status, check-in time  |
| Business identity | QRCode must be unique. Each BookingSeat may generate at most one Ticket.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Valid → Checked-In/Used. Invalid or cancelled states may be used when necessary.  |

**Entity: Payment** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Records a payment attempt made for a Booking.  |
| Key business attributes | Booking, payment method, amount, transaction reference, status, created date, paid date  |
| Business identity | TransactionRef identifies the transaction returned by the payment provider where applicable.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending → Success or Failed. A Booking may have multiple payment attempts but only one successful payment.  |

**Entity: F\&B Item** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a food, drink, or combo item available for purchase during online or counter booking.  |
| Key business attributes | Name, description, item type (Food / Drink / Combo), price, image, status  |
| Business identity | F\&BItemID uniquely identifies each F\&B item.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive. Only Active F\&B items are available for selection.  |

**Entity: Booking F\&B** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents an F\&B item selected as part of a Booking.  |
| Key business attributes | Booking, F\&B item, quantity, unit price, subtotal  |
| Business identity | BookingF\&BID uniquely identifies each selected F\&B entry in a Booking.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Exists while associated with the Booking. No independent lifecycle is required.  |

**Entity: Promotion** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a marketing promotion created by Manager that may issue one or more Vouchers.  |
| Key business attributes | Name, description, start date, end date, status  |
| Business identity | PromotionID uniquely identifies a promotion.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Upcoming → Active → Expired/Inactive according to configured dates and status.  |

**Entity: Voucher** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents a discount code that may be applied to eligible Bookings.  |
| Key business attributes | Promotion, required membership rank, voucher code, discount type, discount value, maximum discount, minimum booking amount, valid period, total usage limit, per-account usage limit, status  |
| Business identity | Voucher code must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Upcoming → Active → Expired/Inactive. Voucher usage is also limited by ValidFrom, ValidTo, TotalUsageLimit, and PerAccountLimit.  |

**Entity: MembershipRank** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Defines Customer membership levels and their loyalty requirements/benefits.  |
| Key business attributes | Rank name, minimum tier points, benefit description, status  |
| Business identity | Rank name must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Active → Inactive. Customer rank is recalculated according to configured tier-point thresholds.  |

 **\=\> Examples may include Member, Silver, Gold, and Platinum.** 

**Entity: News** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Represents cinema news or promotional content created by Staff and reviewed by Manager before publication.  |
| Key business attributes | Creating Staff, reviewing Manager Account, title, content, thumbnail, status, creation/update/submission/review/publication timestamps, rejection reason  |
| Business identity | NewsID uniquely identifies each news article.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Draft → Pending → Published; Pending → Rejected; Rejected may be edited and submitted again; Published may later become Archived.  |

**Entity: SystemSetting** 

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Stores configurable system-wide business parameters controlled by Admin.  |
| Key business attributes | Setting key, setting value, description, updating Account, update time  |
| Business identity | SettingKey must be unique.  |
| Status / lifecycle | Settings remain active until their values are updated. No separate lifecycle is required.  |

 **\=\> Examples include seat-hold duration, booking-reminder time, loyalty-point rules, rank rules, and VAT rate if used.** 

### **3.3 Data Business Rules** {#3.3-data-business-rules}

## 

| ID  | Rule | Description | Enforced On |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-01**  | Unique username  | No two accounts may have the same username.  | Account creation/update  |
| **BR-02**  | Unique email  | No two accounts may have the same email address.  | Registration, account update  |
| **BR-03**  | Unique phone number  | A phone number may belong to only one account.  | Registration, profile update  |
| **BR-04**  | Email verification required  | A new Customer account is activated only after successful email/OTP verification.  | Customer registration  |
| **BR-05** | Current password verification  | An authenticated user must provide the correct current password before changing to a new password.  | Change Password  |
| **BR-06** | Active account authentication  | Only an active account may successfully log in.  | Login  |
| **BR-07** | Showtime requires active movie  | A showtime may only be created for a movie that is available/active in the system.   | Showtime creation  |
| **BR-08** | Showtime requires active room  | A showtime must be assigned to an active cinema room.  | Showtime creation  |
| **BR-09** | No room schedule overlap  | Two showtimes assigned to the same room must not overlap in time.  | Showtime create/update  |
| **BR-10** | Seat belongs to room  | A seat selected for a showtime must belong to the room assigned to that showtime.  | Seat selection  |
| **BR-11** | No double-booked seat  | The same Seat must not be simultaneously Held or Booked by more than one active Booking for the same Showtime.  | Booking, seat confirmation  |
| **BR-12** | Seat hold expiration  | Selected seats are held only for the configured seat-hold duration. If payment is not completed, the hold expires.  | Online booking  |
| **BR-13** | Booking requires seat  | A ticket booking must contain at least one valid seat.  | Booking creation  |
| **BR-14** | One showtime per booking  | All movie tickets in one booking must belong to the same showtime.  | Booking creation  |
| **BR-15** | F\&B is optional  | Selecting F\&B items is optional and is not required to complete a ticket booking.   | Online/Counter booking  |
| **BR-16** | Final booking amount  | Final payable amount equals ticket subtotal plus selected F\&B subtotal minus valid discounts, plus applicable tax if enabled.  | Booking summary/payment  |
| **BR-17** | Voucher validity period  | A voucher may only be used between its ValidFrom and ValidTo dates.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-18** | Voucher active status  | Only vouchers with an active/usable status may be applied.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-19** | Voucher usage limit  | A Voucher cannot be applied after its configured TotalUsageLimit has been reached.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-20** | Voucher conditions  | A Voucher may only be applied when the Booking satisfies its configured minimum booking amount and membership rank requirements, if applicable.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-21** | One voucher per booking  | Only one voucher may be applied to a booking at a time.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-22** | Successful payment required  | A booking becomes Confirmed/Paid only after successful payment confirmation.  | Payment  |
| **BR-23** | Ticket requires successful payment  | A digital ticket/QR code may only be generated for a successfully paid booking.  | Ticket generation  |
| **BR-24** | Payment amount consistency  | The amount of a successful Payment must equal the final payable amount of its associated Booking.  | Payment confirmation  |
| **BR-25** | Failed payment does not issue ticket  | Failed or incomplete payment must not produce a valid ticket.  | Payment  |
| **BR-26** | Unique ticket/QR identifier  | Every issued Ticket must have a unique QRCode.  | Ticket generation  |
| **BR-27** | Ticket single use  | A valid ticket may be successfully checked in only once.  | Ticket verification  |
| **BR-28** | Ticket belongs to showtime  | Ticket information must correspond to the booked movie, showtime, room and seat.  | Ticket generation/verification  |
| **BR-29** | Customer data ownership  | Customer may view only their own profile, bookings, tickets and transaction history.  | Customer account functions  |
| **BR-30** | Review eligibility  | A Customer may submit a MovieReview only for a Movie associated with at least one successfully paid Booking by that Customer.  | Submit Movie Review  |
| **BR-31** | Loyalty points after successful payment  | Loyalty points are added only after an eligible payment is successfully completed.  | Payment/Loyalty  |
| **BR-32** | Automatic membership rank  | Customer membership rank is automatically determined from TierPoints and the configured MembershipRank thresholds.  | Loyalty  |
| **BR-33** | Rank-based benefits  | Available loyalty benefits/vouchers depend on the Customer's current membership rank and configured rules.  | Loyalty  |
| **BR-34** | Customer cannot edit loyalty data  | Customer may view but cannot manually modify loyalty points or membership rank.  | Loyalty Information  |
| **BR-35** | No customer refund/cancellation  | A Customer cannot request cancellation or refund after a successful payment under the current system scope.  | Booking/Payment  |
| **BR-36** | Staff ticket verification  | A Ticket may transition from Valid to Checked-In only if its QRCode is valid, it belongs to the corresponding Showtime, and it has not previously been checked in.  | Ticket verification  |
| **BR-37** | Historical transaction preservation  | Completed booking and payment transaction records must remain available for history/reporting purposes.  | Booking/Transaction data  |
| **BR-38** | Voucher per-account usage limit  | A Customer cannot use the same Voucher more times than its configured PerAccountLimit.  | Apply Voucher  |
| **BR-39** | Unique seat within room  | A seat identifier or position must be unique within the same Room.  | Seat layout management  |
| **BR-40** | Age rating eligibility  | A Customer must satisfy the Movie's age-rating requirement when an age restriction applies.  | Booking / Ticket verification  |
| **BR-41** | One successful payment per booking  | A Booking may have multiple Payment attempts, but at most one Payment may have Success status.  | Payment  |
| **BR-42** | Online booking requires customer  | An ONLINE Booking must be associated with an authenticated Customer.  | Online booking  |
| **BR-43** | Counter booking requires staff  | A COUNTER Booking must be associated with the Staff member processing the sale. Customer association is optional.  | Counter booking  |
| **BR-44** | MovieGenre uniqueness  | The same Genre must not be assigned to the same Movie more than once.  | Movie management  |
| **BR-45** | News approval before publication  | News may become Published only after it has been approved by an Account with the Manager role.  | News approval  |
| **BR-46** | Pending news restriction  | News in Pending status cannot be modified until it is approved or rejected.  | News management  |
| **BR-47** | Published news visibility  | Only News with Published status may be visible to Guest and Customer.  | News display  |
| **BR-48** | Rejected news resubmission  | Rejected News may be edited and submitted again for Manager approval.  | News management  |
| **BR-49** | Unique system setting key  | Each SystemSetting must have a unique SettingKey.  | System configuration  |
| **BR-50** | Ticket price calculation | Ticket unit price \= Showtime base ticket price × SeatType price multiplier, rounded to the nearest 1,000 VND. | Ticket pricing, booking |
| **BR-51** | Price snapshot | BookingSeat and Booking F\&B store the unit price at booking time. Later price or multiplier changes do not affect existing Bookings. | Pricing, F\&B, booking |
| **BR-52** | Room deactivation | A Room that has upcoming Scheduled Showtimes cannot be deactivated. | Room management |
| **BR-53** | No hard delete with history | Seat Types and Seats that are referenced by Booking history cannot be deleted; they can only be deactivated / marked Unavailable. | Seat type & seat layout |
| **BR-54** | Showtime with bookings | Movie, Room and start time of a Showtime cannot be changed, and the Showtime cannot be stopped, once it has Held or Paid Bookings. | Showtime management |
| **BR-55** | Showtime end time | Showtime end time \= start time \+ Movie duration. A new Showtime must start in the future. | Showtime management |

## **4\. User Requirements** {#4.-user-requirements}

### **4.1 Actors** {#4.1-actors}

An actor represents a role played by external entities that interact with the Cinema Management System (not an individual). Actors are identified based on the system’s five main roles — Guest, Customer, Staff, Manager, and Admin — and reconciled with the Use Case diagram. Non-human actors are added for external services that interact with the System, including the Payment Gateway and Email Service 

| \# | Actor | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Guest | Human actor. A user who is not logged in . Guests can view the homepage, browse the movie list, View Movie Information, and check out promotions and news, as well as register for an account or log in to the system. |
| 2 | Customer | Human actor. Inherits all Guest capabilities (generalization). Can select seats, book tickets, make payments, receive digital tickets with QR codes, view booking and transaction history, view loyalty information, submit reviews, and update profile information.  |
| 3 | Staff | Human actor. Handles counter sales and ticket-checking operations, including customer lookup, movie and showtime search, seat availability checking,ticket and food & beverage booking processing , ticket printing, and QR code ticket checking  |
| 4 | Manager | Human actor. Manages movies, rooms and seat information, showtimes, ticket pricing, food and beverage information, promotions and vouchers. Can also request reports and monitor cinema operations, revenue, and statistics  |
| 5 | Admin | Human actors with the highest system privileges. Manages customer, staff, and manager accounts, roles, permissions, account status, and system configuration.  |
| 6 | Payment Gateway | External system actor. Processes payment requests from the Cinema Management System and returns payment results  |
| 7 | Email Service | External system actor. Sends email notifications requested by the Cinema Management System and returns the delivery result.  |

#### ***4.4.1Footnotes***

* **¹ Own data only:** Customer may view or update only data associated with their own Account, Customer profile, Booking, Payment, Ticket, and Membership information.  
* **² Member lookup only:** Staff may view limited Customer, Voucher, and Membership information required for member lookup and counter sales. Staff cannot modify Customer loyalty information.  
* **³ Counter operation only:** Staff may create Bookings and process Payments only for counter sales handled by Staff.  
* **⁴ Online booking operation only:** Customer may access Room/Seat information required for booking and may create and pay only for their own online Booking.  
* **⁵ Reporting / monitoring only:** Manager may view Booking and Payment information only for operational monitoring, reports, and statistics. Manager cannot modify completed transactions.  
* **⁶ Eligible voucher only:** Customer may view and apply only Vouchers that satisfy validity, usage limit, booking amount, and MembershipRank conditions.  
* **⁷ Eligible review only:** Customer may create a MovieReview only when the review eligibility conditions are satisfied.  
* **⁹ Registration only:** Guest may create only a Customer Account through the Register Account flow and must complete email OTP verification before the Account becomes Active.

### **5.2 External API Inventory** {#5.2-external-api-inventory}

| \# | API Name | Calling Path | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Payment Gateway API | Cinema System → Payment Gateway | Sends payment information to an external payment provider and allows Customers to complete online payment for movie bookings. |
| 2 | Payment Callback / Webhook API | Payment Gateway → Cinema System | Receives payment transaction results from the payment provider and updates the booking and payment status accordingly. |
| 3 | Email Service API | Cinema System → Email Service | Sends booking confirmation emails, digital ticket information, password reset emails, and other required system notifications to Customers. |

### **5.3 Background Job Inventory** {#5.3-background-job-inventory}

| \# | Job Name | Group | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Release expired seat reservations | Scheduled | Periodically releases temporarily held seats when the Customer does not complete payment within the allowed booking time. |
| 2 | Cancel expired unpaid bookings | Scheduled | Periodically checks unpaid bookings that have exceeded the payment time limit and automatically changes their status to cancelled. |
| 3 | Update expired promotions and vouchers | Scheduled | Periodically checks promotion and voucher expiration dates and automatically marks expired promotions or vouchers as inactive. |
| 4 | Clean up expired password reset tokens | Scheduled | Periodically removes or invalidates password reset tokens that have exceeded their expiration time. |
| 5 | Clean up old temporary booking data | Scheduled | Daily removes expired temporary booking or transaction data that is no longer required by the system. |
| 6 | Booking Reminder Notification  | Scheduled  | Periodically checks upcoming confirmed bookings and sends reminder notifications to Customers before the showtime according to the configured reminder time.  |

## **6\. Use Case Specifications** {#6.-use-case-specifications}

### **6.1 Guest** {#6.1-guest}

#### ***6.1.1. Register account***

| UC ID and Name: | UC05 — Register Account |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Nguyen Hoang Hung | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Guest | **Secondary Actors:** | Email Service  |
| **Trigger:** | Guest selects **Create Account**. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows Guest to create a new Customer account by providing valid registration information and completing email OTP verification.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. Guest is not authenticated. 2\. The registration function is available. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | A verified Customer account exists with status Active. Guest can proceed to Sign In.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Guest selects Create Account. 2\. System displays the registration form. 3\. Guest enters full name, email, phone number, username, password, and confirm password. 4\. System checks required fields, formats, and lengths. 5\. System checks for duplicate usernames, emails, and phone numbers. 6\. System stores the password as a hash and creates an account with Pending Verification status. 7\. System sends an OTP to the registered email. 8\. Guest enters the OTP. 9\. System checks the OTP and its validity period. 10\. System changes the account status to Active. 11\. System displays a successful registration and verification message. 12\. Guest can go to Login.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1 (Step 4): A required field is missing → identify the field to be completed. A2 (Step 4): Email, phone number, username, or password has an invalid format → display the corresponding requirements for correction. A3 (Step 4): Confirm password does not match → request re-entry. A4 (Step 5): Email / phone number / username already exists → report the duplicate and request a change. A5 (Step 7): OTP delivery fails → notify and allow resending. A6 (Step 9): OTP is incorrect → allow another attempt if attempts remain. A7 (Step 9): OTP has expired → request a new code. A8 (Step 9): More than 5 incorrect OTP attempts → invalidate the OTP and require a new code. A9: Guest requests another OTP → send only after 60 seconds and invalidate the old OTP.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | E1: The account cannot be saved due to a database error → report failure and do not show a registration success message. E2: Authentication service / system error → record a technical log, suggest retrying, and do not activate the account automatically  |  |  |
| **Priority:**  | High  |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:**  | Medium  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:**  | BR-REG-01: Full name is required, 2–100 characters, not only spaces; Unicode letters, spaces, and valid punctuation in names are accepted. BR-REG-02: Username is required, 5–30 characters; only unaccented letters (A–Z, a–z), digits (0–9), and underscore (\_); no spaces; must be unique, with case-insensitive duplicate checking. BR-REG-03: Email is required, up to 254 characters, with a valid local-part@domain structure; no spaces; must be normalized before comparison and unique. BR-REG-04: Phone number is required, exactly 10 digits, starts with 0, no other characters; must be unique. This rule applies to Vietnamese phone numbers. BR-REG-05: Password is required, 8–64 characters, with at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 digit, and 1 special character; no spaces. BR-REG-06: Confirm password is required and must match the password exactly. BR-REG-07: Duplicate Username, Email, or Phone values are not allowed, including for disabled accounts; enforce uniqueness at the database level. BR-REG-08: Passwords must be stored using a dedicated salted password hash (e.g., Argon2id or bcrypt), never in plain text. BR-REG-09: OTP contains 6 digits, is valid for 5 minutes, and can be used once; up to 5 attempts per OTP. BR-REG-10: A new OTP request must be at least 60 seconds after the most recent send; a new OTP invalidates the old one. BR-REG-11: Create the account as Pending Verification; switch to Active only after a valid OTP. BR-REG-12: Pending Verification accounts cannot log in.   |  |  |
| **Other Information:**  | Email verification is part of the Register Account flow. Character limits, validity periods, and attempt limits in the business rules are additional proposals.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:**  | 1\. Database connection works. 2\. Registration and email delivery services work. 3\. Users provide information they own.   |  |  |

#### ***6.1.2*** **View Movie List**

| UC ID and Name: | UC01 — View Movie List |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Nguyen Hoang Hung | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Guest, Customer | **Secondary Actors:** | N/A |
| **Trigger:** | User accesses the **Home Page** or **Movie List** page. |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allows users to view movies that are approved for public display.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. The Movie List page is publicly accessible and does not require login. 2\. The system can retrieve the movie list and its categories.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The system displays the available public movie list; no data is changed.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. User opens the Home Page or Movie List page. 2\. System retrieves movies approved for public display. 3\. System displays movies under the configured categories, such as Now Showing, Coming Soon, and Special (if available). 4\. User views the movie list.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1: No movies are available for public display → show an appropriate empty-list message. A2: A configured category has no movies → show an empty state for that category, without displaying unrelated movies.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:**  | E1: The system cannot retrieve movie data → display an error message and allow the user to retry.  |  |  |
| **Priority:**  | High  |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:**  | High  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:**  | BR-ML-01: Display only movies marked for public display; movies with Stopped status must not appear. BR-ML-02: Group movies according to configured categories: Now Showing, Coming Soon, and Special (if available). BR-ML-03: If no publicly available movies exist, display an appropriate empty-list message. BR-ML-04: A category with no movies must not be filled with movies from another category.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:**  | This is a public function; Guests do not need authentication.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:**  | Movie information, categories, and statuses are correctly maintained by the system.  |  |  |

| **Priority:**  | Medium  |  |  |

BR-PN-02: The current time must fall within \[start date, end date\] using the configured system time zone; start/end boundary handling must be consistent. BR-PN-03: When configuring a promotion, the end date must not be earlier than the start date. BR-PN-04: News must have Published status and a publication time that is not in the future. BR-PN-05: Inactive / expired promotions and unpublished news must not be publicly displayed. BR-PN-06: When one content type has no data, the other type must still be displayed normally.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:**  | This is a public function and does not require login.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:**  | Promotion statuses and validity schedules, as well as news publication schedules, are managed correctly.  |  |  |

BR-MI-06: Display only showtimes that remain available and belong to the selected movie. BR-MI-07: Missing optional data must not cause the entire Use Case to fail.  |  |  |

| **Description:** | View showtimes by date and filter by movie, genre, age rating, or room type.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. The showtime function is active. 2\. The system can retrieve movie, room, and showtime data and their relationships. 3\. Login is not required just to view; there may be no matching showtimes.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | Matching showtimes or a no-results state are displayed; no data is changed.  |  |  |

System filters showtimes for the selected date. 6\. User may select a movie, genre, age rating, or room type. 7\. System applies all selected filters. 8\. User views the results.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1: No showtimes exist on the selected date → show a no-showtimes message. A2: No showtimes match the filters → show a no-results message. A3: User changes the date or filters → update the list. A4: A related movie or room becomes unavailable → the showtime can no longer be selected.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:**  | E1: Date or filter value is invalid → request a new selection. E2: Showtimes cannot be loaded → notify the user and allow retrying.  |  |  |
| **Priority:**  | High  |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:**  | High  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:**  | BR-ST-01: A showtime must be linked to an existing movie and room. BR-ST-02: Display only showtimes with available status; do not display canceled or disabled showtimes. BR-ST-03: The linked movie must be public and not Stopped; the linked room must remain active. BR-ST-04: The selected date must be valid; showtimes that have ended must not be presented as bookable. BR-ST-05: The end time of a showtime must be later than its start time. BR-ST-06: Two showtimes in the same room must not overlap in time (a constraint checked when managing showtimes). BR-ST-07: Movie, genre, age rating, and room type filters must use values existing in the system. BR-ST-08: When multiple filters are applied, a showtime must satisfy every criterion. BR-ST-09: An empty list must show a message; showtimes that do not match the filters must not be displayed.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:**  | Guests/Customers can proceed to booking from a valid showtime; Staff can use showtime information when selling tickets at the counter.   |  |  |
| **Assumptions:**  | Movie, room, and showtime data are maintained correctly; statuses are updated promptly.  |  |  |

| **Preconditions:** | 1\. The customer has a registered account. 2\. The customer is not currently logged in.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | 1\. The customer is authenticated successfully. 2\. A valid login session is created. 3\. Customers can access protected Customer functions.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Customer opens the Login page. 2\. The system displays the login form. 3\. Customer enters email/username and password. 4\. The customer submits the form. 5\. The system validates the credentials. 6\. The system checks the account status. 7\. The system creates an authenticated session. 8\. The system redirects Customer to the homepage.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1. Invalid credentials:** System displays an error and allows Customer to try again. **A2. Customer selects Forgot Password:** Continue to UC09 — Forgot / Reset Password.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1. Account inactive/locked:** System denies login and displays the corresponding message. **E2. System error:** Login cannot be completed; system displays an error message.  |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High – Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | High  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Only active accounts with valid credentials can log in.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Authentication information must not expose whether a specific email/account exists when authentication fails.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | The customer account has already been registered.  |  |  |

User enters and confirms the new password. 10\. System validates the password. 11\. System updates the password. 12\. System displays a success message.  |  |  |

| **Priority:** | High – Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Low  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | OTP/reset link must have a limited validity period. The new password must satisfy the password policy.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Email Service is used only for account verification/recovery.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | User can access the registered email address.   |  |  |

#### ***6.2.5 Book Tickets Online*** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC11 — Book Tickets Online   |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Hoang Son Ha | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Customer  | **Secondary Actors:** | N/A  |
| **Trigger:** | The customer starts the online ticket booking process.  |  |  |
| **Description:** | The customer creates a movie ticket booking by selecting a movie and showtime, seats, optional food and beverage items, and an optional voucher before proceeding to payment.   |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. The customer is logged in. 2\. Movies and showtimes are available. 3\. The booking period for the selected showtime is still open.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | 1\. A pending booking is created. 2\. Selected seats are temporarily held. 3\. Final payable amount is calculated. 4\. Booking is ready for UC12 — Make Payment.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Customer starts booking. 2\. Customer selects a movie and showtime. 3\. System displays the seat map. 4\. Customer selects available seat(s). 5\. System validates and temporarily holds the selected seats. 6\. System displays available Food & Beverage items. 7\. Customer optionally selects Food & Beverage items. 8\. Customer optionally enters/selects a voucher. 9\. System validates the voucher if provided. 10\. System calculates the final payable amount. 11\. System displays the booking summary. 12\. Customer confirms the booking. 13\. System creates a Pending booking. 14\. Customer proceeds to UC12 — Make Payment.    |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1. Showtime unavailable:** Customer selects another showtime. **A2. Seat unavailable:** System refreshes the seat map and Customer selects another seat. **A3. Skip F\&B:** Booking continues without F\&B. **A4. Skip Voucher:** Booking continues without discount. **A5. Invalid voucher:** System displays the reason and uses the original payable amount.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1. Seat-hold failure:** System informs Customer and requires seat selection again. **E2. Booking creation failure:** No booking is created and held seats are released.  |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High – Must Have   |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | High  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | A seat cannot be assigned to more than one active booking for the same showtime. Seat holding expires according to configured seat-hold time. F\&B and voucher are optional.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Includes **Select Movie & Showtime** and **Select Seats**; **Select Food & Beverage** and **Apply Voucher** are optional extensions in the UC Diagram.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Pricing, seats, showtimes, vouchers and F\&B data are available.    |  |  |

#### ***6.2.6 Make Payment***  

| UC ID and Name: | UC12 — Make Payment    |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Hoang Son Ha | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Customer  | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway  |
| **Trigger:** | Customer proceeds to payment for a Pending booking.   |  |  |
| **Description:** | Customer pays for a booking through the integrated Payment Gateway.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. A valid Pending booking exists. 2\. Final payable amount has been calculated. 3\. Selected seats are still held.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **Success:** Booking becomes Confirmed/Paid, selected seats become booked and digital ticket/QR is generated. **Failure:** No valid digital ticket is issued.   |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. System displays booking summary and final payable amount. 2\. Customer selects a supported payment method. 3\. Customer confirms payment. 4\. System sends payment information to Payment Gateway. 5\. Payment Gateway processes the transaction. 6\. Payment Gateway returns a successful result. 7\. System records the transaction. 8\. System changes booking status to Paid/Confirmed. 9\. System marks the selected seats as booked. 10\. System generates digital ticket and QR code. 11\. System adds applicable loyalty points and recalculates Customer rank. 12\. System triggers the booking confirmation email. 13\. System displays payment success and ticket information.   |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1. Payment failed:** System displays failure and allows another payment attempt while the seat hold remains valid. **A2. Customer cancels payment:** System returns Customer to the booking/payment page.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1. Payment Gateway unavailable:** System displays an unavailable-payment message. **E2. Seat hold expires before successful payment:** Booking cannot be completed and Customer must select seats again.  |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High – Must Have   |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | High  |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | Digital ticket can only be issued after successful payment. A Payment Gateway result must be verified before confirming the booking.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | After successful payment, the system sends booking/ticket information through Email Service. .  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Payment Gateway is available and configured correctly.     |  |  |

| UC ID and Name: | UC19 Counter Ticket Sales  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Nguyễn Hải Đăng | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Staff   | **Secondary Actors:** | Payment Gateway  |
| **Trigger:** | Staff opens the Counter Ticket Sales screen upon a customer's request to purchase tickets directly at the cinema.  |  |  |
| **Description:** | Staff selects a movie, showtime, available seats, optional food & beverage (F\&B) items, applies membership discounts/vouchers, and processes payment for counter sales.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1.Staff is logged in and authorized to perform counter sales. 2.Movie, showtime, seat, and F\&B data are available in the system.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | 1.Booking status becomes paid/confirmed . 2.Selected seats are marked as booked . 3.Digital/Physical ticket and payment receipt are generated.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1.Staff opens the Counter Ticket Sales screen. 2.Staff searches and selects the requested movie and showtime. 3.System displays the interactive seat map for the selected room. 4.Staff selects available seat(s) requested by the customer. 5.System validates and temporarily holds the selected seats. 6.Staff optionally selects F\&B items if requested. 7.Staff optionally searches for customer account by phone number/email to apply member benefits/points. 8.System calculates the final payable amount and displays booking summary  9.Staff selects payment method (Cash or VNPay QR Code) and confirms payment. 10.Payment Gateway/System processes payment and updates booking status to Paid/Confirmed.  11.System generates tickets with unique QR codes and triggers printing for tickets and receipt.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1. Payment Failure / Customer Cancels: Staff cancels or retries the transaction. Temporarily held seats are released if canceled. A2. Skip F\&B / Member Lookup: Staff proceeds to checkout without adding F\&B items or linking a customer profile.   |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | E1. Seat Selection Conflict**:** Selected seat becomes unavailable (booked online concurrently). System refreshes seat map and prompts Staff to select another seat.  |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High – Must Have |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | High |  |  |

| **Priority:** | Medium |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Medium |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-17, BR-18, BR-19, BR-20, BR-21, BR-38   |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | BR-17 to BR-21 and BR-38 are checked when a Voucher is applied during booking. Expired Promotions/Vouchers are updated automatically by JOB-03.  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | Membership Ranks are configured by Admin.  |  |  |

System validates the Manager's action. 8\. System updates the news article status. 9\. System displays a confirmation message and refreshes the news list.  |  |  |

| **Frequency of Use:** | Medium |  |  |

#### ***6.5.4 Manage System Rules & Configuration*** 

##### 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-39— Manage System Rules & Configuration  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Created By:** | Le Thi Kim Oanh | **Date Created:** | 22/09/2026 |
| **Primary Actor:** | Admin | **Secondary Actors:** | N/A |
| **Trigger:** | Admin selects **Manage System Rules & Configuration**.   |  |  |
| **Description:** | Allow Admin to manage system-level rules and configuration settings.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | 1\. Admin is logged in. 2\. Admin has permission to manage system rules and configuration.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The selected system rule or configuration setting is successfully updated and saved.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | 1\. Admin opens **Manage System Rules & Configuration**. 2\. System displays the available system rules and configuration settings. 3\. Admin selects a rule or configuration setting. 4\. System displays its current value. 5\. Admin enters or selects a new value. 6\. System validates the new value. 7\. Admin confirms the change. 8\. System saves the updated value. 9\. System displays a success message.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | **A1.** Configure Voucher Validity: Admin sets or updates the voucher start date and expiration date. **A2**. Configure Voucher Quantity: Admin sets the number of vouchers that can be issued for a voucher program. **A3**. Configure Voucher Usage Limit: Admin sets the maximum number of times a voucher can be used. **A4.** Configure Voucher Conditions: Admin configures conditions such as minimum booking amount or required membership rank. **A5**. Configure Membership Rank Thresholds: Admin defines the point thresholds required for membership ranks such as Silver, Gold, and Diamond. **A6.** Configure Membership Benefits: Admin configures the benefits associated with each membership rank, where supported by the system.   |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | **E1**. Invalid Date Range: System rejects the voucher validity period when the entered dates are invalid. **E2**. Invalid Quantity: System rejects the voucher quantity when the value is invalid. **E3**. Invalid Usage Limit: System rejects an invalid voucher usage limit. **E4**. Invalid Membership Threshold: System rejects an invalid or inconsistent membership point threshold. **E5**. Invalid Configuration Value: System rejects a value that does not satisfy the configured validation rules. **E6**. Duplicate SettingKey: System rejects the configuration because each `SettingKey` must be unique.     |  |  |
| **Priority:** | High – Must Have  |  |  |
| **Frequency of Use:** | Low |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-17, BR-18, BR-19, BR-20, BR-32, BR-33, BR-49.  |  |  |
| **Other Information:** | Admin configures system-level business rules rather than performing day-to-day voucher or membership operations. Voucher creation/management and customer loyalty activities are handled by their respective functions  |  |  |
| **Assumptions:** | 1\. The system provides configuration fields for voucher and membership rules. 2\. Admin has permission to modify system rules and configuration. 3\. Voucher validity, quantity, usage limits, and conditions are validated before being saved. 4\. Membership rank thresholds are configured using loyalty points. 5\. Membership ranks such as Silver, Gold, and Diamond are predefined by the system or configurable by Admin. 6\. Each system configuration has a unique `SettingKey`.  |  |  |

# **II. Functional Requirements** {#ii.-functional-requirements}

## **1\. User Authentication** {#1.-user-authentication}

### **1.1 User Register** {#1.1-user-register}

![][image15]

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| ***Personal Information*** |  |
| Full Name | Data type: String. Initial value: blank. Required field. Allows the user to enter their full name. |
| Email | Data type: String. Initial value: blank. Required field. Must follow a valid email format and must not duplicate an existing email in the system. |
| Phone Number | Data type: Numeric String. Initial value: blank. Must follow the supported phone number format. |
| ***Security Information*** |  |
| Password | Data type: Password. Initial value: blank. Required field. The password is hidden by default and must satisfy the system password policy. |
| Show/Hide Password | Data type: Icon/Button. Default state: Hide Password. Allows the user to show or hide the entered password. |
| Confirm Password | Data type: Password. Initial value: blank. Required field. Must match the Password field. |

### **1.2 User Login** {#1.2-user-login}

![][image16]

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| ***Login Information*** |  |
| Email | Data type: String. Initial value: blank. Required field. Must follow a valid email format. |
| Password | Data type: Password. Initial value: blank. Required field. The password is hidden by default. |
| Show/Hide Password | Data type: Icon/Button. Allows the user to switch between showing and hiding the password. |
| Remember Me | Data type: Checkbox. Default value: unchecked. Allows the system to maintain the user session according to the configured authentication policy. |
| ***Navigation and Actions*** |  |
| Forgot Password | Data type: Hyperlink. Navigates to the Forgot / Reset Password screen. |
| Login | Data type: Button. When clicked, the system validates the Email and Password. If valid, the user is authenticated and logged into the system. |

## **2\. Customer** {#2.-customer}

### **2.1 Movie Discovery** {#2.1-movie-discovery}

**2.1.1 Homepage**

![][image17] 

**Brief Description**  
The Homepage provides Customers with an overview of available movies in the cinema system. Customers can search for movies, view currently showing and upcoming movies, open movie details, or start the ticket booking process directly from the movie cards.

**Mapped Use Cases:**

* UC01 – View Movie List  
* UC02 – View Movie Information  
* UC03 – View Showtimes

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Featured Movie | Displays a highlighted movie including poster/banner, title, genre, duration, age rating, and short description. |
| Now Showing | Displays movies that are currently available for screening. |
| Coming Soon | Displays movies that will be available in the future. |
| Movie Poster | Data type: Image. Displays the movie poster and can be used to open the Movie Details screen. |
| Movie Title | Data type: Text/Link. Displays the title of the movie. |
| Genre | Data type: Text/List. Displays one or more genres associated with the movie. |
| Duration | Data type: Integer/Minutes. Displays the movie runtime. |
| Age Rating | Data type: Text. Displays the movie age classification. |
| Release Date | Data type: Date. Displays the official movie release date. |
| View Details | Data type: Button/Link. Navigates to the Movie Details screen. |
| Book Ticket | Data type: Button. Starts the online booking flow for the selected movie. |

**2.1.2 Movie List** 

![][image18]

**Brief Description**  
The Movie List screen displays available and upcoming movies in the system. Customers can search for movies and narrow the displayed results using movie status, genre, age rating, and sorting options. Customers can open movie details or start the booking process from the selected movie.

**Mapped Use Case:**  
UC01 – View Movie List

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Movie Status | Data type: Dropdown. Values: All, Now Showing, Coming Soon. Default: All. |
| Genre | Data type: Dropdown. Displays all active genres. Default: All Genres. |
| Age Rating | Data type: Dropdown. Allows filtering movies by age classification. |
| Sort By | Data type: Dropdown. Allows sorting by release date, title, popularity, or other supported criteria. |
| Movie Poster | Data type: Image. Displays the poster of the movie. |
| Movie Title | Data type: Text/Link. Displays the movie title. |
| Genre Information | Displays one or more movie genres. |
| Duration | Data type: Integer/Minutes. Displays movie runtime. |
| Age Rating | Displays the movie age classification. |
| Release Date | Data type: Date. Displays the movie release date. |
| View Details | Data type: Button/Link. Opens Movie Details. |
| Book Ticket | Data type: Button. Starts the online booking process. |

**2.1.3 Movie Details** 

![][image19]

**Brief Description**  
The Movie Details screen provides detailed information about a selected movie. Customers can review movie information, watch the trailer, browse available showtimes, start the ticket booking process, and view customer reviews.

**Mapped Use Cases:**  
UC02 – View Movie Information  
UC03 – View Showtimes  
UC16 – Submit Movie Review

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Movie Poster | Displays the official movie poster. |
| Movie Title | Displays the title of the selected movie. |
| Movie Description | Data type: Long Text. Displays the movie synopsis. |
| Genre | Displays one or more associated genres. |
| Duration | Displays movie runtime in minutes. |
| Release Date | Displays the official release date. |
| Director | Displays the movie director. |
| Cast | Displays main actors and actresses. |
| Language | Displays movie language. |
| Age Rating | Displays movie age classification. |
| Movie Rating | Displays the average customer rating. |
| Watch Trailer | Opens the trailer screen. |
| View Showtimes | Opens available showtimes for the movie. |
| Book Ticket | Starts online booking. |
| Review List | Displays customer reviews. |
| Write Review | Opens the review form when the Customer is eligible. |

**2.1.4 Watch Trailer** 

![][image20]

**Brief Description**  
The Watch Trailer screen allows Customers to play the official trailer of the selected movie using standard video playback controls.

**Mapped Use Case:**  
UC02 – View Movie Information

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Movie Title | Displays the movie whose trailer is being played. |
| Trailer Player | Data type: Video Player. Displays the official trailer. |
| Play / Pause | Starts or pauses video playback. |
| Progress Bar | Displays playback progress and allows seeking when supported. |

| Full Screen | Displays the trailer in full-screen mode. |

## **6\. Background Job Inventory** {#6.-background-job-inventory}

### **6.1 Release Expired Seat Reservations (JOB-01)**  {#6.1-release-expired-seat-reservations-(job-01)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — periodically. 

***Purpose***: Periodically releases temporarily held seats when the Customer does not complete payment within the allowed booking time. 

***Processing steps*****:**

1. Find BookingSeat records with status Held.  
2. Check whether HeldUntil has expired.  
3. Change expired held seats to Released/Expired.  
4. Make the seats available for other bookings.  
5. Keep the related Booking status consistent with the seat-hold state.

***Failure behavior*****:**

* If the database cannot be accessed, the job records the failure and retries on the next scheduled execution.   
* If no expired seat reservations are found, the job completes without making changes. 

### **6.2 Cancel Expired Unpaid Bookings (JOB-02)**  {#6.2-cancel-expired-unpaid-bookings-(job-02)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — periodically. 

***Purpose***: Periodically checks unpaid bookings that have exceeded the payment time limit and automatically changes their status to cancelled/expired. 

***Processing steps:***

1. Find Bookings with status Pending.  
2. Check whether the allowed payment period has expired.  
3. Mark expired unpaid Bookings as Expired or Cancelled.  
4. Release any seats still being held by those Bookings.  
5. Ensure no Ticket is generated for the expired Booking.

**Failure behavior:**

* If the job cannot update a Booking, the Booking remains unchanged until the next execution.  
* If no expired unpaid Bookings exist, the job completes normally.

### **6.3 Update Expired Promotions and Vouchers (JOB-03)**  {#6.3-update-expired-promotions-and-vouchers-(job-03)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — periodically. 

***Purpose***: Periodically checks Promotion and Voucher expiration dates and automatically makes expired Promotions or Vouchers unavailable. 

***Processing steps:***

1. Find active Promotions whose EndDate has passed.  
2. Change their status to Expired/Inactive.  
3. Find active Vouchers whose ValidTo has passed  
4. Change their status to Expired/Inactive.  
5. Ensure expired Promotions and Vouchers cannot be applied to new Bookings.

**Failure behavior:**

* If expiration data cannot be updated, the job records the failure and retries during the next execution.  
* If there are no expired Promotions or Vouchers, no data is changed.

### **6.4 Clean Up Expired Password Reset Tokens (JOB-04)**  {#6.4-clean-up-expired-password-reset-tokens-(job-04)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — periodically. 

***Purpose***: Removes or invalidates password-reset tokens or OTP data that have exceeded their expiration time.  

***Processing steps:***

1. Find expired password-reset tokens or OTP records.  
2. Mark them invalid or remove them according to the implementation.  
3. Prevent expired tokens from being used to reset an account password.

**Failure behavior:**

* If cleanup cannot be completed, expired tokens remain unusable based on expiration validation and are processed again during the next job execution.  
* If no expired tokens exist, the job completes normally.

### **6.5 Clean Up Old Temporary Booking Data (JOB-05)**  {#6.5-clean-up-old-temporary-booking-data-(job-05)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — daily. 

***Purpose***: Removes expired temporary booking or transaction data that is no longer required by the system. 

***Processing steps:***

1. Find temporary booking data that has already expired.  
2. Verify that the data is no longer required for an active Booking or Payment.  
3. Remove eligible temporary data.  
4. Preserve completed Booking and Payment history required by BR-37.

**Failure behavior:**

* If cleanup fails, existing data remains unchanged and the job retries during the next scheduled execution.  
* Completed historical Booking and Payment records must not be removed.

### **6.6 Booking Reminder Notification (JOB-06)**  {#6.6-booking-reminder-notification-(job-06)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — periodically according to the configured reminder time. 

***Purpose***: Periodically checks upcoming confirmed Bookings and sends reminder notifications to Customers before the Showtime. 

***Processing steps:***

1. Retrieve upcoming Bookings with status Paid/Confirmed.  
2. Check the Showtime start time against the configured booking-reminder time.  
3. Identify Bookings that are due for a reminder.  
4. Request Email Service to send a booking reminder to the Customer.  
5. Avoid sending duplicate reminders for the same Booking when already sent.

**Failure behavior:**

* If Email Service is unavailable, the reminder is not marked as successfully sent and may be retried later.  
* If no upcoming Booking requires a reminder, the job completes without sending notifications.

## **7\. External API Inventory** {#7.-external-api-inventory}

### **7.1 Payment Gateway API (API-01)** {#7.1-payment-gateway-api-(api-01)}

| *URL* | POST: /api/v1/payments/create |
| :---- | :---- |
| ***Purpose*** | Creates an online payment request for a movie booking and redirects the Customer to the selected payment gateway. |
| ***Caller*** | Cinema Management System |
| ***Auth*** | Yes – authenticated Customer access token and payment gateway credentials/signature |

### **7.2 VNPay Webhook (API-02)** {#7.2-vnpay-webhook-(api-02)}

| *URL* | POST: /api/v1/payments/webhook/vnpay |
| :---- | :---- |
| ***Purpose*** | Receives payment confirmation from VNPay and updates the related booking and payment transaction status. |
| ***Caller*** | VNPay Payment Gateway |
| ***Auth*** | Yes – HMAC-SHA512 signature validation |

### **7.3 Email Service API (API-03)** {#7.3-email-service-api-(api-03)}

| *URL* | POST: /api/v1/notifications/email |
| :---- | :---- |
| ***Purpose*** | Sends booking confirmations, digital ticket information, and password reset emails to Customers. |
| ***Caller*** | Cinema Management System |
| ***Auth*** | Yes – API key or service authentication token |

# **III. Requirement Appendix** {#iii.-requirement-appendix}

## **1\. Business Rules** {#1.-business-rules}

| GBR-ID | Rule Statement | Applies To | Rationale | Enforced By |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GB-01 | A seat can only be booked by one customer for the same showtime.  | Seat Booking  | Prevents duplicate seat reservations.  | System automatically when confirming a booking  |
| GB-02 | Customers can only select seats that are available for the selected showtime.  | Seat Selection  | Ensures accurate seat availability.  | System automatically when displaying and selecting seats  |
| GB-03 | A booking is confirmed only after the payment is completed successfully.  | Booking, Payment  | Prevents unpaid bookings from being treated as valid tickets.  | System automatically after payment confirmation  |
| GB-04 | Each confirmed booking generates a unique ticket with a QR code.  | Ticket  | Allows staff to identify and validate tickets.  | System automatically after payment confirmation  |
| GB-05 | A ticket QR code can only be successfully validated once for admission.  | Ticket Validation  | Prevents reuse of the same ticket.  | System automatically when Staff scans the QR code  |
| GB-06 | A showtime must belong to one movie and one cinema room.  | Showtime Management  | Ensures each screening has a valid movie and room assignment.  | System automatically when Manager creates or updates a showtime  |
| GB-07 | Two showtimes in the same room must not have overlapping screening times.  | Showtime Management  | Prevents scheduling conflicts.  | System automatically when Manager creates or updates a showtime  |
| GB-08 | Only authenticated Customers can create online bookings, make payments, view booking history, and submit ratings or reviews.  | Customer Functions  | Protects customer transactions and personal information.  | System authorization  |
| GB-09 | Customers can only rate or review movies associated with their completed bookings.  | Rating & Review  | Ensures reviews are submitted by customers who booked the movie.  | System automatically when submitting a review  |
| GB-10 | Voucher codes can only be applied when they are valid, active, and meet their usage conditions.  | Voucher, Booking  | Prevents invalid discounts.  | System automatically during checkout  |
| GB-11 | Only authorized roles can access management functions according to their assigned permissions.  | Admin, Manager, Staff  | Prevents unauthorized access to internal functions.  | Role-based access control  |
| GB-12 | A deactivated account cannot sign in to the system.  | Authentication  | Prevents inactive users from accessing the system.  | System automatically during sign-in  |

## **2\. System Messages** {#2.-system-messages}

| \# | Message code | Message Type | Context | Content |
| :---: | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | MSG1 | In line  | System/server operation fails  | *Something went wrong. Please try again later.*  |
| 2 | MSG02 | In red, under the text box  | Required field is empty  | *This field is required.*  |
| 3 | MSG03 | Toast message  | Login successfully  | Login successfully.  |
| 4 | MSG04 | In line  | Username/email or password is incorrect  | *Incorrect email or password. Please try again.*  |
| 5 | MSG05 | Toast message | Registration successfully  | *Registration successful. Please verify your email.*  |
| 6 | MSG06 | In red, under the text box | Email format is invalid  | *Invalid email address.*  |
| 7 | MSG07 | In line | Selected seat is no longer available  | *This seat is no longer available. Please select another seat.*  |
| 8 | MSG08 | Toast message  | Booking created successfully  | *Booking successful.*  |
| 9 | MSG09 | Toast message  | Payment completed successfully  | *Payment successful.*  |
| 10 | MSG10 | Toast message  | Payment fails  | *Payment failed. Please try again.*  |
| 11 | MSG11 | In line  | Voucher is invalid or expired  | *Invalid or expired voucher code.*  |
| 12 | MSG12 | Toast message  | Ticket is successfully validated  | *Ticket validated successfully.*  |
| 13 | MSG13 | Warning message  | Ticket has already been used  | *This ticket has already been used.*  |
| 14 | MSG14 | Toast message  | Data is created successfully  | *Created successfully.*  |
| 15 | MSG15 | Toast message  | Data is updated successfully  | *Updated successfully.*  |
| 16 | MSG16 | Toast message  | Data is deleted successfully  | *Deleted successfully.*  |
| 17 | MSG17 | In line  | Showtime conflicts with another showtime  | *The selected room already has a conflicting showtime.*  |
| 18 | MSG18 | Toast message  | Review submitted successfully  | *Review submitted successfully.*  |
| 19 | MSG19 | In line  | User does not have permission  | *You do not have permission to perform this action.*  |

## **3\. Other Requirements** {#3.-other-requirements}

| ID | Category | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| OR-01  | Responsive Design  | The web application shall support common desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes.  |
| OR-02 | Browser Compatibility  | The system shall support modern versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari.  |
| OR-03 | Security  | Passwords shall be securely hashed before being stored in the database.  |
| OR-04 | Authorization  | The system shall enforce role-based access control for Customer, Staff, Manager, and Admin functions.  |
| OR-05 | Data Validation  | User input shall be validated before being processed or stored.  |
| OR-06 | Payment  | Online payment shall be processed through the integrated VNPay payment service or the project's simulated VNPay environment.  |
| OR-07 | Ticket  | Confirmed bookings shall provide customers with a digital ticket containing booking information and a QR code.  |
| OR-08 | Performance  | Common user operations should respond within an acceptable time under normal operating conditions.  |
| OR-09 | Error Handling  | The system shall display clear error messages without exposing sensitive system or database information.  |
| OR-10 | Data Consistency  | Seat, booking, payment, and ticket status shall remain consistent throughout the booking process.  |
